probe_stimulus.source: F-SI18 five-case convergence-cliff probe, compatibility-adapted only to the shared F-MR12/F-MR13 request generation
compatibility_edits: remove exactly one later-generation request%physical%macropore_active=.false. write because F-MR12/F-MR13 share the older request type and the same test sets swmacro=0
synchronize legacy time and numerical globals to the already identical request values consumed by the shared F-MR12/F-MR13 adapter
assert zero alternative/band solver calls so this probe isolates the TRIDAG seam

discarded_probe_interpretation.reason: F-SI18/F-SI19 use a later HeadCalc/request contract generation with explicit physical, numerical, time and parameter arguments, while F-MR12/F-MR13 share the older runtime contract. The failed cross-generation probe therefore mixed solver-seam and contract-generation differences and is not evidence of a production regression.

qualified_capabilities: production-bound HeadCalc execution of the F-MR13 reference TRIDAG seam under the exact F-MR12/F-MR13 shared runtime contract
baseline plus four small nonzero top-flux perturbations with all five cases converged
bitwise F-MR12 predecessor equivalence at O0 and O2
repeat-run and O0/O2 deterministic identity for the five-case probe
not_admitted: F-SI15 explicit physical-option contract composition into F-MR runtime
prescribed-bottom-head behavior beyond separately qualified routes
band-fallback production-bound nonzero behavior beyond the existing direct F-SI19 oracle
new physics or new numerical controls
BALANCED, THROUGHPUT or FALLBACK execution classes
architecture_note: F-VQ24 does not qualify the older F-MR12/F-MR13 implicit macropore-global contract as the desired SWAP5 architecture. Physical-option explicitness remains a separate composition responsibility under the architecture invariants.

release.restriction: F-PE may consume only the exact F-MR13 production postimage and the qualified five-case F-VQ24 scope unless a broader workload receives separate admission.

claim_limit: F-VQ24 proves only that the F-MR13 production-bound reference linear TRIDAG seam is bitwise equivalent to the SWAP 4.3.1 Thomas reference when inserted into its exact F-MR12 predecessor runtime for the qualified five-case HeadCalc workload. It does not broaden physics, solver-policy, performance or execution-class admission.
